notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); this package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null), no hardware was attached, and no ROS graph, Flatland process, simulator run or hardware run is claimed. At the original bootstrap run the card showed helper: null and blocked_on [helper:ros]; the orchestrator's explicit bootstrap instruction says to use RosDriver here, so the package was scaffolded with --kind ros and task.json was not edited. It is a configuration-only ROS 1 RosDriver over rosbridge, mode simulated, risk R0, device_kind world.sim; there is no Python native class and no native.py. The card's entry_symbols list is empty, so there was no entry symbol to verify; the pinned endpoints and types were read directly from the clone: /clock with rosgraph_msgs/Clock (flatland_server/src/timekeeper.cpp:53-54), the relative pause service with std_srvs/Empty (flatland_server/src/service_manager.cpp:63 and flatland_server/include/flatland_server/service_manager.h:53) and the relative resume service (flatland_server/src/service_manager.cpp:65). Both Empty services are acknowledged with success={"path": "$", "equals": {}}. The pause action is input-free with safe_state=True and the same /pause service is bound as the simulator stop; the runtime latches in software first, and the described safe state is paused physics (World::Update skips the plugin before-step hook, the Box2D step and Timekeeper::StepTime while IsPaused is true, flatland_server/src/world.cpp:101-110), not a zero-velocity command and not a physical emergency stop. World::IsPaused is also true while the internal marker manager manipulates (flatland_server/src/world.cpp:333-340), so a held clock sample alone does not prove the pause flag. A namespaced deployment must expose the resolved /pause and /resume endpoints; the upstream names are recorded as source_name. Scope and not covered: only /clock observation and pause/resume are served; world stepping, reset, rendering, TF, poses, laser/odometry and every other Flatland plugin or topic are NOT COVERED. The package does not start or validate a ROS graph, and rosbridge parameter access, actions, QoS, authentication and reconnection are outside the helper. The fake is a ROS-free RecordingRosTransport: it answers the declared subscribe and call_service messages with placeholder clock samples and placeholder service acknowledgements, and it models an application-predicate failure through fail_pause_application. Its numbers are test data (# placeholder), not facts. Fidelity is F0 for the deployed event-driven recording fake: engine analytic:ROS recording fake (no physics), determinism none, timestep_ms 0, realtime_factor 0 (no pacing), reset none, no snapshot/restore or advancing clock. Upstream timing defaults are source facts only. No Limit is declared because no action has a numeric input and the clone states no numeric bound for the clock or the Empty services; consequently site-limits.example.json is not needed. Warnings kept from the last gate run: G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE is expected because no actuating capability declares a limit, so there is nothing for the out-of-limit probe to test; the message says every other CL3 test passed. There are no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. test_driver.py runs eight cases including the gate, clock observation, stock pause/resume, no fresh paused clock before deadline, service wire calls, application failure, ROS service failure and the e-stop latch. The clone was left unmodified (G1 passed); no network, pip install or upstream execution was used.
